types.name: Client
types.description:
A client (cliente) — a person the firm represents. Owned by the `main` subgraph
as a single flat entity; extended here to expose the support contacts linked to
that client.

This is a plain federated entity, NOT an `@interfaceObject`. The `main` subgraph
collapsed the old `JudgmentCreditor` / `Heir` type hierarchy into one flat
`Client` row with one id space, so the bare id Chatwoot stores
(`contact_links.client_id`) resolves directly. An `@interfaceObject` would need
the concrete implementation type to be resolvable from that bare id — it was not,
and composition failed with "no subgraph can be reached to resolve the
implementation type of @interfaceObject type Person".

fields.name: contacts
fields.description: Support contacts linked to this client.

types.name: Contact
types.description:
A contact: an end customer or person the account communicates with. Belongs to
the current account and may be linked to a `Client` in the `main` subgraph.

A federated `@key` entity so other subgraphs (e.g. the `main` subgraph's
`ServiceRecord`) can reference a contact by id; the generic `resolve_reference`
in `chatwoot_schema.rb` resolves it via `Contact.find_by(id:)`.

fields.name: additionalAttributes
fields.description: Additional system attributes (e.g. social profiles, geo).

fields.name: blocked
fields.description: Whether the contact is blocked.

fields.name: client
fields.description:
The linked client, or null if the contact is not linked. Resolved as a federated
entity from the `main` subgraph — read `client { id }` for the id, and any other
`Client` field (name, cpf, kind, …) straight off the merged entity. `kind` tells
you whether the client is an exequente or a herdeiro.

fields.name: clientId
fields.description: The linked client's id, without resolving the federated entity.

fields.name: contactInboxes
fields.description: The inbox associations (source ids) through which this contact is reachable.

types.name: Conversation

A customer-support conversation: a thread of messages between a contact and the
agents of an inbox. Scoped to the current account; an agent only sees
conversations in inboxes they can access (admins see all).

types.name: ID
types.description: Represents a unique identifier that is Base64 obfuscated. It is often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"VXNlci0xMA=="`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.

types.name: Message
types.description:
A single message within a conversation. May be an incoming customer message, an
outgoing agent reply, a private internal note, or a system activity entry.

fields.description:
Rendering/content type, as an integer: 0 = text, 1 = input_text,
2 = input_textarea, 3 = input_email, 4 = input_select, 5 = cards, 6 = form,
7 = article, 8 = incoming_email, 9 = input_csat, 10 = integrations,
11 = sticker, 12 = voice_call.

1 = outgoing (from an agent/bot), 2 = activity (system event),
3 = template (pre-approved channel template).

fields.name: private
fields.description:
Whether this is a private internal note, visible only to agents (not the
contact).

fields.name: senderId
fields.description: Id of the sender (a User, AgentBot or Contact, depending on senderType).

fields.name: sourceId

fields.name: status
fields.description:

types.name: Team
types.description:
A team groups agents within an account for assignment and routing.

Federated entity shared with the organization (`server`) subgraph: the SAME
logical team is owned there as the canonical `Team` (with its labor unions and
platform metadata). The two subgraphs are joined on `platformTeamId` — the
platform team id (`public.team.id`), mirrored here as `chatwoot.teams.platform_team_id`.
`id` stays the Chatwoot team id so `assignConversationToTeam` is unaffected;
`name`/`description` are `@shareable` because both subgraphs resolve them.

subgraph's canonical `Team`. Null for Chatwoot teams not synced from a

fields.name: workingHours

The team's business hours (platform calendar). One entry per configured
weekday; empty until set via `setTeamWorkingHours`. Contributed by the Chatwoot
subgraph and resolved on the federated `Team` via the `platformTeamId` join.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
